offer.serviceDescription: Full-service reefer and cold-chain freight brokerage for F&B shippers: dry van, reefer FTL, reefer LTL, frozen and multi-temp, backed by a 100,000+ vetted-carrier network, with continuous temperature monitoring and real-time GPS on every reefer load.
offer.uniqueAngle: Be the no-risk backup broker on a painful lane: second-source reefer capacity with continuous temperature monitoring and full carrier vetting on every load, so on-time and temperature-safe stays covered even when primary capacity tightens.
guarantees: Continuous temperature monitoring + real-time GPS on every reefer load
Every reefer carrier is FSMA and CARB compliant and fully vetted (FMCSA authority, insurance, safety record, continuous identity verification)
99.9% claims-free track record across all modes
Equipment from sprinter / reefer-LTL to 53-ft and multi-temp trailers, ambient (55F) down to deep frozen (-20F)
24/7 dispatch, live tracking, hourly updates, EDI, same-day invoicing, hard-copy POD, and a dedicated rep who knows the freight
problemsSolved: OTIF retail chargebacks (often cited around $100 to $500 per shipment or a percentage of PO value) that the logistics director is personally graded on
Perishable, must-arrive-by delivery windows that are tight and non-negotiable
Temperature-claim disputes when the data trail is incomplete
Reefer-LTL underservice and 2026 reefer capacity tightness, reliable backup coverage
offer.quantifiableResults: 100,000+ vetted carriers; 99.9% claims-free delivery rate across all modes; FMCSA licensed and bonded, BBB accredited; full modal coverage including dry van, reefer, frozen and multi-temp.
process: Quick lane review: share your toughest reefer lane, volume, and delivery windows
We match vetted, FSMA/CARB-compliant reefer capacity and confirm coverage
Every load ships with continuous temperature monitoring + real-time GPS, 24/7 dispatch
POD and same-day invoicing; we scale into more lanes as the backup proves out
offer.frontEndOffer: A free reefer lane review plus an OTIF chargeback-exposure read on your toughest temperature-controlled lane. A no-obligation second-source capacity check, not a hard sell.
offer.exampleEmail:
{{first_name}},

Saw that {{company}} ships a lot of temperature-controlled freight on tight retail delivery windows, where one late or short reefer load turns into an OTIF chargeback that lands on you.

We come in as a vetted, FSMA-compliant backup on the one or two reefer lanes where your primary runs tight, so the hard lanes stay covered and you are not switching anyone.

Happy to send a quick read on your toughest reefer lane, what it is running against the current market and where the OTIF exposure sits, yours to keep. Worth a look?

items.q: "Aren't you just a broker reselling my freight?"
items.a: Lead with carrier vetting plus temperature monitoring on every load: vetted backup capacity with a real person accountable, not a faceless reseller.

items.q: "We already have carriers / a primary broker."
items.a: That is exactly the fit. We come in as your second-source / backup on tight reefer lanes and peak overflow, not a rip-and-replace.
Rates depend on the lane, commodity, and equipment, so we will not throw out a cold number. Quick lane review or a short call and we will scope it properly.
items.ask: Any rate or margin guidance you want us to work within, or keep it lane-review only?

items.q: "Can you actually hold temperature, and prove it?"
items.a: Continuous temperature monitoring and real-time GPS on every reefer load, with FSMA and CARB-compliant vetted carriers.
items.ask: Do your carriers provide downloadable temp logs / an audit trail, or is it live-monitoring only? (We need to know before we claim it.)

items.a: Yes, we can reference relevant named accounts once you confirm which are OK to use, anonymized if you prefer (for example a national beverage brand).
items.ask: OK to reference Anheuser-Busch / Lindsay Windows in outreach (even anonymized)?

items.q: How big is your carrier network?
items.a: A vetted network with FMCSA authority, insurance, and safety checks on every carrier before dispatch.
items.ask: Your site shows both 10,000+ and 100,000+ for the carrier network. Which number should we use in outreach?

items.q: "Which F&B should we focus on, and how big?"
items.a: Default is all cold-chain F&B (frozen, dairy, meat & poultry, produce, beverage), mid-market 50 to 2,000 employees, national.
items.ask: Narrow the sub-vertical, strongest lanes/regions, size floor, and manufacturers-only vs include distributors?
